title.value: Precise Accuracy / Robustness Tradeoffs in Regression: Case of General Norms
title.justification: The title of the paper is mentioned clearly at both the beginning and in the header/footer of the document.
title.quote: Precise Accuracy / Robustness Tradeoffs in Regression: Case of General Norms

analysis.description: This paper investigates the impact of test-time adversarial attacks on linear regression models, exploring the accuracy and robustness tradeoffs in such scenarios. It provides a theoretical framework to compute optimal robustness levels in relation to standard predictive performance and extends previous works by applying to general norms and covariance matrices.

type.justification: The paper primarily focuses on theoretical analysis and provides mathematical formulations for understanding the tradeoffs between robustness and accuracy in linear regression under adversarial attacks.
type.quote: "This work mostly considers the following question:...Is it possible to be robust while being accurate?"

name.justification: The paper is centered around understanding and analyzing the tradeoffs between robustness and accuracy in the presence of adversarial attacks.
name.quote: ...our results apply to arbitrary covariance structures and attack norms.

name.justification: The paper specifically examines these tradeoffs in the context of linear regression models.
name.quote: In this paper, we investigate the impact of test-time adversarial attacks on linear regression models...

name.justification: Overall, this research contributes to the broader field of machine learning with its focus on understanding model performance under adversarial scenarios.
name.quote: Machine learning models are known to be highly sensitive to small perturbations known as adversarial examples...

name.justification: Ridge regression is referred to frequently as a model that achieves optimal robustness under certain conditions.
name.quote: In the special case of Euclidean-norm attacks, it is a ridge estimator, and we recover a simplified formulation of the result obtained in (Xing et al., 2021).

is_contributed.justification: The paper uses existing models like ridge regression to explain their robustness under adversarial attacks instead of contributing a new model.
is_contributed.quote: In the special case of Euclidean-norm attacks, it is a ridge estimator, and we recover a simplified formulation of the result obtained in (Xing et al., 2021).

is_executed.justification: The paper does not provide evidence about executing or experimenting with the models on any hardware.
is_executed.quote: Our findings are empirically confirmed with simple experiments that represent a variety of settings.

is_compared.justification: The paper compares ridge regression and other models theoretically to analyze robustness and accuracy tradeoffs under adversarial attacks.
is_compared.quote: Their results show a tradeoff between standard and adversarial risk for adversarial training.
